sanskrit_shloka:
यो वा पुरे सोऽहमिति प्रतीतो बुद्ध्या प्रकॢप्तस्तमसातिमूढया ।
तस्यैव निःशेषतया विनाशे ब्रह्मात्मभावः प्रतिबन्धशून्यः ॥ ३0१ ॥
transliteration:
yo vā pure so'hamiti pratīto buddhyā prakḷptastamasātimūḍhayā |
tasyaiva niḥśeṣatayā vināśe brahmātmabhāvaḥ pratibandhaśūnyaḥ || 301 ||
translation: That which has been created by the Buddhi extremely deluded by Nescience, and which is perceived in this body as 'I am such and such' - when that egoism is totally destroyed, one attains an unobstructed identity with Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which has been created by the Buddhi extremely deluded by Nescience, and which is perceived in this body as 'I am such and such' - when that egoism is totally destroyed, one attains an unobstructed identity with Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मानन्दनिधिर्महाबलवताहंकारघोराहिना संवेष्ट्यात्मनि रक्ष्यते गुणमायाइश्चण्डेस्त्रिभिर्मस्तकैः ।
विज्ञानाख्यमहासिना श्रुतिमता विच्छिद्य शीर्षत्रयं निर्मूल्याहिमिमं निधिं सुखकरं धीरोऽनुभोक्तुंक्षमः ॥ ३0२ ॥
transliteration:
brahmānandanidhirmahābalavatāhaṃkāraghorāhinā saṃveṣṭyātmani rakṣyate guṇaMāyāiścaṇḍestribhirmastakaiḥ |
vijñānākhyamahāsinā śrutimatā vicchidya śīrṣatrayaṃ nirmūlyāhimimaṃ nidhiṃ sukhakaraṃ dhīro'nubhoktuṃkṣamaḥ || 302 ||
translation: The treasure of the Bliss of Brahman is coiled round by the mighty and dreadful serpent of egoism, and guarded for its own use by means of its three fierce hoods consisting of the three Guṇas. Only the wise man, destroying it by severing its three hoods with the great sword of realisation in accordance with the teachings of the Śrutis, can enjoy this treasure which confers bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The treasure of the Bliss of Brahman is coiled round by the mighty and dreadful serpent of egoism, and guarded for its own use by means of its three fierce hoods consisting of the three Guṇas. Only the wise man, destroying it by severing its three hoods with the great sword of realisation in accordance with the teachings of the Śrutis, can enjoy this treasure which confers bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
यावद्वा यत्किंचिद्विषदोषस्फूर्तिरस्ति चेद्देहे ।
कथमारोग्याय भवेत्तद्वदहन्तापि योगिनो मुक्त्यै ॥ ३0३ ॥
transliteration:
yāvadvā yatkiṃcidviṣadoṣasphūrtirasti ceddehe |
kathamārogyāya bhavettadvadahantāpi yogino muktyai || 303 ||
translation: As long as there is a trace of poisoning left in the body, how can one hope for recovery? Similar is the effect of egoism on the Yogi’s Liberation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As long as there is a trace of poisoning left in the body, how can one hope for recovery? Similar is the effect of egoism on the Yogi’s Liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहमोऽत्यन्तनिवृत्त्या तत्कृतनानाविकल्पसंहृत्या ।
प्रत्यक्तत्त्वविवेकादिदमहमस्मीति विन्दते तत्त्वम् ॥ ३0४ ॥
transliteration:
ahamo'tyantanivṛttyā tatkṛtanānāvikalpasaṃhṛtyā |
pratyaktattvavivekādidamahamasmīti vindate tattvam || 304 ||
translation: Through the complete cessation of egoism, through the stoppage of the diverse mental waves due to it, and through the discrimination of the inner Reality, one realises that Reality as 'I am This'.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the complete cessation of egoism, through the stoppage of the diverse mental waves due to it, and through the discrimination of the inner Reality, one realises that Reality as 'I am This'.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहंकारे कर्तर्यहमिति मतिं मुञ्च सहसा विकारात्मन्यात्मप्रतिफलजुषि स्वस्थितिमुषि ।
यदध्यासात्प्राप्ता जनिमृतिजरादुःखबहुला प्रतीचश्चिन्मूर्तेस्तव सुखतनोः संसृतिरियम् ॥ ३0५ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃkāre kartaryahamiti matiṃ muñca sahasā vikārātmanyātmapratiphalajuṣi svasthitimuṣi |
yadadhyāsātprāptā janimṛtijarāduḥkhabahulā pratīcaścinmūrtestava sukhatanoḥ saṃsṛtiriyam || 305 ||
translation: Give up immediately thy identification with egoism, the agent, which is by its nature a modification, is endued with a reflection of the Self, and diverts one from being established in the Self – identifying thyself with which thou hast come by this relative existence, full of the miseries of birth, decay and death, though thou art the Witness, the Essence of Knowledge and Bliss Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Give up immediately thy identification with egoism, the agent, which is by its nature a modification, is endued with a reflection of the Self, and diverts one from being established in the Self – identifying thyself with which thou hast come by this relative existence, full of the miseries of birth, decay and death, though thou art the Witness, the Essence of Knowledge and Bliss Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
सदैकरूपस्य चिदात्मनो विभोर् आनन्दमूर्तेरनवद्यकीर्तेः ।
नैवान्यथा क्वाप्यविकारिणस्ते विनाहमध्यासममुष्य संसृतिः ॥ ३0६ ॥
transliteration:
sadaikarūpasya cidātmano vibhor ānandamūrteranavadyakīrteḥ |
naivānyathā kvāpyavikāriṇaste vināhamadhyāsamamuṣya saṃsṛtiḥ || 306 ||
translation: But for thy identification with that egoism there can never be any transmigration for thee who art immutable and eternally the same, the Knowledge Absolute, omnipresent, the Bliss Absolute, and of untarnished glory.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: But for thy identification with that egoism there can never be any transmigration for thee who art immutable and eternally the same, the Knowledge Absolute, omnipresent, the Bliss Absolute, and of untarnished glory.

sanskrit_shloka:
तस्मादहंकारमिमं स्वशत्रुं भोक्तुर्गले कण्टकवत्प्रतीतम् ।
विच्छिद्य विज्ञानमहासिना स्फुटं भुङ्क्ष्वात्मसाम्राज्यसुखं यथेष्टम् ॥ ३0७ ॥
transliteration:
tasmādahaṃkāramimaṃ svaśatruṃ bhokturgale kaṇṭakavatpratītam |
vicchidya vijñānamahāsinā sphuṭaṃ bhuṅkṣvātmasāmrājyasukhaṃ yatheṣṭam || 307 ||
translation: Therefore destroying this egoism, thy enemy - which appears like a thorn sticking in the throat of a man taking meal – with the great sword of realisation, enjoy directly and freely the bliss of thy own empire, the majesty of the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore destroying this egoism, thy enemy - which appears like a thorn sticking in the throat of a man taking meal – with the great sword of realisation, enjoy directly and freely the bliss of thy own empire, the majesty of the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
ततोऽहमादेर्विनिवर्त्य वृत्तिं संत्यक्तरागः परमार्थलाभात् ।
तूष्णीं समास्स्वात्मसुखानुभूत्या पूर्णात्मना ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पः ॥ ३0८ ॥
transliteration:
tato'hamādervinivartya vṛttiṃ saṃtyaktarāgaḥ paramārthalābhāt |
tūṣṇīṃ samāssvātmasukhānubhūtyā pūrṇātmanā brahmaṇi nirvikalpaḥ || 308 ||
translation: Checking the activities of egoism etc., and giving up all attachment through the realisation of the Supreme Reality, be free from all duality through the enjoyment of the Bliss of Self, and remain quiet in Brahman, for thou hast attained thy infinite nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Checking the activities of egoism etc., and giving up all attachment through the realisation of the Supreme Reality, be free from all duality through the enjoyment of the Bliss of Self, and remain quiet in Brahman, for thou hast attained thy infinite nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
समूलकृत्तोऽपि महानहं पुनः व्युल्लेखितः स्याद्यदि चेतसा क्षणम् ।
संजीव्य विक्षेपशतं करोति नभस्वता प्रावृषि वारिदो यथा ॥ ३0९ ॥
transliteration:
samūlakṛtto'pi mahānahaṃ punaḥ vyullekhitaḥ syādyadi cetasā kṣaṇam |
saṃjīvya vikṣepaśataṃ karoti nabhasvatā prāvṛṣi vārido yathā || 309 ||
translation: Even though completely rooted out, this terrible egoism, if revolved in the mind even for a moment, returns to life and creates hundreds of mischiefs, like a cloud ushered in by the wind during the rainy season.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Even though completely rooted out, this terrible egoism, if revolved in the mind even for a moment, returns to life and creates hundreds of mischiefs, like a cloud ushered in by the wind during the rainy season.

sanskrit_shloka:
निगृह्य शत्रोरहमोऽवकाशः क्वचिन्न देयो विषयानुचिन्तया ।
स एव संजीवनहेतुरस्य प्रक्षीणजम्बीरतरोरिवाम्बु ॥ ३१0 ॥
transliteration:
nigṛhya śatrorahamo'vakāśaḥ kvacinna deyo viṣayānucintayā |
sa eva saṃjīvanaheturasya prakṣīṇajambīratarorivāmbu || 310 ||
translation: Overpowering this enemy, egoism, not a moment’s respite should be given to it by thinking on the sense-objects. That is verily the cause of its coming back to life, like water to a citron tree that has almost dried up.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Overpowering this enemy, egoism, not a moment’s respite should be given to it by thinking on the sense-objects. That is verily the cause of its coming back to life, like water to a citron tree that has almost dried up.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहात्मना संस्थित एव कामी विलक्षणः कामयिता कथं स्यात् ।
अतोऽर्थसन्धानपरत्वमेव भेदप्रसक्त्या भवबन्धहेतुः ॥ ३११ ॥
transliteration:
dehātmanā saṃsthita eva kāmī vilakṣaṇaḥ kāmayitā kathaṃ syāt |
ato'rthasandhānaparatvameva bhedaprasaktyā bhavabandhahetuḥ || 311 ||
translation: He alone who has identified himself with the body is greedy after sense-pleasures. How can one, devoid of the body-idea, be greedy (like him)? Hence the tendency to think on the sense-objects is verily the cause of the bondage of transmigration, giving rise to an idea of distinction or duality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He alone who has identified himself with the body is greedy after sense-pleasures. How can one, devoid of the body-idea, be greedy (like him)? Hence the tendency to think on the sense-objects is verily the cause of the bondage of transmigration, giving rise to an idea of distinction or duality.

sanskrit_shloka:
कार्यप्रवर्धनाद्बीजप्रवृद्धिः परिदृश्यते ।
कार्यनाशाद्बीजनाशस्तस्मात्कार्यं निरोधयेत् ॥ ३१२ ॥
transliteration:
kāryapravardhanādbījapravṛddhiḥ paridṛśyate |
kāryanāśādbījanāśastasmātkāryaṃ nirodhayet || 312 ||
translation: When the effects are developed, the seed also is observed to be such, and when the effects are destroyed, the seed also is seen to be destroyed. Therefore one must subdue the effects.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the effects are developed, the seed also is observed to be such, and when the effects are destroyed, the seed also is seen to be destroyed. Therefore one must subdue the effects.

sanskrit_shloka:
वासनावृद्धितः कार्यं कार्यवृद्ध्या च वासना ।
वर्धते सर्वथा पुंसः संसारो न निवर्तते ॥ ३१३ ॥
transliteration:
vāsanāvṛddhitaḥ kāryaṃ kāryavṛddhyā ca vāsanā |
vardhate sarvathā puṃsaḥ saṃsāro na nivartate || 313 ||
translation: Through the increase of desires selfish work increases, and when there is an increase of selfish work, there is an increase of desire also. And man’s transmigration is never at an end.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the increase of desires selfish work increases, and when there is an increase of selfish work, there is an increase of desire also. And man’s transmigration is never at an end.

sanskrit_shloka:
संसारबन्धविच्छित्त्यै तद्द्वयं प्रदहेद्यतिः ।
वासनावृद्धिरेताभ्यां चिन्तया क्रियया बहिः ॥ ३१४ ॥
transliteration:
saṃsārabandhavicchittyai taddvayaṃ pradahedyatiḥ |
vāsanāvṛddhiretābhyāṃ cintayā kriyayā bahiḥ || 314 ||
translation: For the sake of breaking the chain of transmigration, the Sannyasin should burn to ashes those two; for thinking of the sense-objects and doing selfish acts lead to an increase of desires.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For the sake of breaking the chain of transmigration, the Sannyasin should burn to ashes those two; for thinking of the sense-objects and doing selfish acts lead to an increase of desires.

sanskrit_shloka:
ताभ्यां प्रवर्धमाना सा सूते संसृतिमात्मनः ।
त्रयाणां च क्षयोपायः सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ॥ ३१५ ॥
transliteration:
सर्वत्र सर्वतः सर्वब्रह्ममात्रावलोकनैः ।
सद्भाववासनादार्ढ्यात्तत्त्रयं लयमश्नुते ॥ ३१६ ॥
translation: 315-316. Augmented by these two, desires produce one’s transmigration. The way to destroy these three, however, lies in looking upon everything, under all circumstances, always, everywhere and in all respects, as Brahman and Brahman alone. Through the strengthening of the longing to be one with Brahman, those three are annihilated.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 315-316. Augmented by these two, desires produce one’s transmigration. The way to destroy these three, however, lies in looking upon everything, under all circumstances, always, everywhere and in all respects, as Brahman and Brahman alone. Through the strengthening of the longing to be one with Brahman, those three are annihilated.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्रियानाशे भवेच्चिन्तानाशोऽस्माद्वासनाक्षयः ।
वासनाप्रक्षयो मोक्षः सा जीवन्मुक्तिरिष्यते ॥ ३१७ ॥
transliteration:
kriyānāśe bhaveccintānāśo'smādvāsanākṣayaḥ |
vāsanāprakṣayo mokṣaḥ sā jīvanmuktiriṣyate || 317 ||
translation: With the cessation of selfish action the brooding on the sense-objects is stopped, which is followed by the destruction of desires. The destruction of desires is Liberation, and this is considered as Liberation-in-life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: With the cessation of selfish action the brooding on the sense-objects is stopped, which is followed by the destruction of desires. The destruction of desires is Liberation, and this is considered as Liberation-in-life.

sanskrit_shloka:
सद्वासनास्फूर्तिविजृम्भणे सति ह्यसौ विलीनाप्यहमादिवासना ।
अतिप्रकृष्टाप्यरुणप्रभायां विलीयते साधु यथा तमिस्रा ॥ ३१८ ॥
transliteration:
sadvāsanāsphūrtivijṛmbhaṇe sati hyasau vilīnāpyahamādivāsanā |
atiprakṛṣṭāpyaruṇaprabhāyāṃ vilīyate sādhu yathā tamisrā || 318 ||
translation: When the desire for realising Brahman has a marked manifestation, the egoistic desires readily vanish, as the most intense darkness effectively vanishes before the glow of the rising sun.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the desire for realising Brahman has a marked manifestation, the egoistic desires readily vanish, as the most intense darkness effectively vanishes before the glow of the rising sun.

sanskrit_shloka:
तमस्तमःकार्यमनर्थजालं न दृश्यते सत्युदिते दिनेशे ।
तथाद्वयानन्दरसानुभूतौ न वास्ति बन्धो न च दुःखगन्धः ॥ ३१९ ॥
transliteration:
tamastamaḥkāryamanarthajālaṃ na dṛśyate satyudite dineśe |
tathādvayānandarasānubhūtau na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ || 319 ||
translation: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

sanskrit_shloka:
तमस्तमःकार्यमनर्थजालं न दृश्यते सत्युदिते दिनेशे ।
तथाद्वयानन्दरसानुभूतौ न वास्ति बन्धो न च दुःखगन्धः ॥ ३१९ ॥
transliteration:
tamastamaḥkāryamanarthajālaṃ na dṛśyate satyudite dineśe |
tathādvayānandarasānubhūtau na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ || 319 ||
translation: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Darkness and the numerous evils that attend on it are not noticed when the sun rises. Similarly, on the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the least trace of misery.

sanskrit_shloka:
दृश्यं प्रतीतं प्रविलापयन्सन् सन्मात्रमानन्दघनं विभावयन् ।
समाहितः सन्बहिरन्तरं वा कालं नयेथाः सति कर्मबन्धे ॥ ३२0 ॥
transliteration:
dṛśyaṃ pratītaṃ pravilāpayansan sanmātramānandaghanaṃ vibhāvayan |
samāhitaḥ sanbahirantaraṃ vā kālaṃ nayethāḥ sati karmabandhe || 320 ||
translation: Causing the external and internal universe, which are now perceived, to vanish, and meditating on the Reality, the Bliss Embodied, one should pass one’s time watchfully, if there be any residue of Prārabdha work left.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Causing the external and internal universe, which are now perceived, to vanish, and meditating on the Reality, the Bliss Embodied, one should pass one’s time watchfully, if there be any residue of Prārabdha work left.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रमादो ब्रह्मनिष्ठायां न कर्तव्यः कदाचन ।
प्रमादो मृत्युरित्याह भगवान्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥ ३२१ ॥
transliteration:
pramādo brahmaniṣṭhāyāṃ na kartavyaḥ kadācana |
pramādo mṛtyurityāha bhagavānbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 321 ||
translation: One should never be careless in one’s steadfastness to Brahman. Bhagavan Sanatkumāra, who is Brahma’s son, has called inadvertence to be death itself.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: One should never be careless in one’s steadfastness to Brahman. Bhagavan Sanatkumāra, who is Brahma’s son, has called inadvertence to be death itself.

sanskrit_shloka:
न प्रमादादनर्थोऽन्यो ज्ञानिनः स्वस्वरूपतः ।
ततो मोहस्ततोऽहंधीस्ततो बन्धस्ततो व्यथा ॥ ३२२ ॥
transliteration:
na pramādādanartho'nyo jñāninaḥ svasvarūpataḥ |
tato mohastato'haṃdhīstato bandhastato vyathā || 322 ||
translation: There is no greater danger for the Jñānin than carelessness about his own real nature. From this comes delusion, thence egoism, this is followed by bondage, and then comes misery.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is no greater danger for the Jñānin than carelessness about his own real nature. From this comes delusion, thence egoism, this is followed by bondage, and then comes misery.

sanskrit_shloka:
विषयाभिमुखं दृष्ट्वा विद्वांसमपि विस्मृतिः ।
विक्षेपयति धीदोषैर्योषा जारमिव प्रियम् ॥ ३२३ ॥
transliteration:
viṣayābhimukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidvāṃsamapi vismṛtiḥ |
vikṣepayati dhīdoṣairyoṣā jāramiva priyam || 323 ||
translation: Finding even a wise man hankering after the sense-objects, oblivion torments him through the evil propensities of the Buddhi, as a woman does her doting paramour.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Finding even a wise man hankering after the sense-objects, oblivion torments him through the evil propensities of the Buddhi, as a woman does her doting paramour.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति ।
आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥ ३२४ ॥
transliteration:
yathāpakṛṣṭaṃ śaivālaṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ na tiṣṭhati |
āvṛṇoti tathā māyā prājñaṃ vāpi parāṅmukham || 324 ||
translation: As moss, even if removed, does not stay away for a moment, but covers the water again, so Māyā or Nescience also covers even a wise man, if he is averse to meditation on the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As moss, even if removed, does not stay away for a moment, but covers the water again, so Māyā or Nescience also covers even a wise man, if he is averse to meditation on the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
लक्ष्यच्युतं चेद्यदि चित्तमीषद् बहिर्मुखं सन्निपतेत्ततस्ततः ।
प्रमादतः प्रच्युतकेलिकन्दुकः सोपानपङ्क्तौ पतितो यथा तथा ॥ ३२५ ॥
transliteration:
lakṣyacyutaṃ cedyadi cittamīṣad bahirmukhaṃ sannipatettatastataḥ |
pramādataḥ pracyutakelikandukaḥ sopānapaṅktau patito yathā tathā || 325 ||
translation: If the mind ever so slightly strays from the Ideal and becomes outgoing, then it goes down and down, just as a play-ball inadvertently dropped on the staircase bounds down from one step to another.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the mind ever so slightly strays from the Ideal and becomes outgoing, then it goes down and down, just as a play-ball inadvertently dropped on the staircase bounds down from one step to another.

sanskrit_shloka:
विषयेष्वाविशच्चेतः संकल्पयति तद्गुणान् ।
सम्यक्संकल्पनात्कामः कामात्पुंसः प्रवर्तनम् ॥ ३२६ ॥
transliteration:
viṣayeṣvāviśaccetaḥ saṃkalpayati tadguṇān |
samyaksaṃkalpanātkāmaḥ kāmātpuṃsaḥ pravartanam || 326 ||
translation: The mind that is attached to the sense-objects reflects on their qualities; from mature reflection arises desire, and after desiring a man sets about having that thing.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The mind that is attached to the sense-objects reflects on their qualities; from mature reflection arises desire, and after desiring a man sets about having that thing.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतः प्रमादान्न परोऽस्ति मृत्युः विवेकिनो ब्रह्मविदः समाधौ ।
समाहितः सिद्धिमुपैति सम्यक् समाहितात्मा भव सावधानः ॥ ३२७ ॥
transliteration:
ataḥ pramādānna paro'sti mṛtyuḥ vivekino brahmavidaḥ samādhau |
samāhitaḥ siddhimupaiti samyak samāhitātmā bhava sāvadhānaḥ || 327 ||
translation: Hence to the discriminating knower of Brahman there is no worse death than inadvertence with regard to concentration. But the man who is concentrated attains complete success. (Therefore) carefully concentrate thy mind (on Brahman).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Hence to the discriminating knower of Brahman there is no worse death than inadvertence with regard to concentration. But the man who is concentrated attains complete success. (Therefore) carefully concentrate thy mind (on Brahman).

sanskrit_shloka:
ततः स्वरूपविभ्रंशो विभ्रष्टस्तु पतत्यधः ।
पतितस्य विना नाशं पुनर्नारोह ईक्ष्यते ॥ ३२८ ॥
transliteration:
tataḥ svarūpavibhraṃśo vibhraṣṭastu patatyadhaḥ |
patitasya vinā nāśaṃ punarnāroha īkṣyate || 328 ||
translation: Through inadvertence a man deviates from his real nature, and the man who has thus deviated falls. The fallen man comes to ruin, and is scarcely seen to rise again.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through inadvertence a man deviates from his real nature, and the man who has thus deviated falls. The fallen man comes to ruin, and is scarcely seen to rise again.

sanskrit_shloka:
संकल्पं वर्जयेत्तस्मात्सर्वानर्थस्य कारणम् ।
जीवतो यस्य कैवल्यं विदेहे स च केवलः यत्किंचित्पश्यतो भेदं भयं ब्रूते यजुःश्रुतिः ॥ ३२९ ॥
transliteration:
saṃkalpaṃ varjayettasmātsarvānarthasya kāraṇam |
jīvato yasya kaivalyaṃ videhe sa ca kevalaḥ yatkiṃcitpaśyato bhedaṃ bhayaṃ brūte yajuḥśrutiḥ || 329 ||
translation: Therefore one should give up reflecting on the sense-objects, which is the root of all mischief. He who is completely aloof even while living, is alone aloof after the dissolution of the body. The Yajur-Veda declares that there is fear for one who sees the least bit of distinction.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore one should give up reflecting on the sense-objects, which is the root of all mischief. He who is completely aloof even while living, is alone aloof after the dissolution of the body. The Yajur-Veda declares that there is fear for one who sees the least bit of distinction.

sanskrit_shloka:
यदा कदा वापि विपश्चिदेष ब्रह्मण्यनन्तेऽप्यणुमात्रभेदम् ।
पश्यत्यथामुष्य भयं तदैव यद्वीक्षितं भिन्नतया प्रमादात् ॥ ३३0 ॥
transliteration:
yadā kadā vāpi vipaścideṣa brahmaṇyanante'pyaṇumātrabhedam |
paśyatyathāmuṣya bhayaṃ tadaiva yadvīkṣitaṃ bhinnatayā pramādāt || 330 ||
translation: Whenever the wise man sees the least difference in the infinite Brahman, at once that which he sees as different through mistake, becomes a source of terror to him.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whenever the wise man sees the least difference in the infinite Brahman, at once that which he sees as different through mistake, becomes a source of terror to him.

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रुतिस्मृतिन्यायशतैर्निषिद्धे दृश्येऽत्र यः स्वात्ममतिं करोति ।
उपैति दुःखोपरि दुःखजातं निषिद्धकर्ता स मलिम्लुचो यथा ॥ ३३१ ॥
transliteration:
śrutismṛtinyāyaśatairniṣiddhe dṛśye'tra yaḥ svātmamatiṃ karoti |
upaiti duḥkhopari duḥkhajātaṃ niṣiddhakartā sa malimluco yathā || 331 ||
translation: He who identifies himself with the objective universe which has been denied by hundreds of Shrutis, Smritis and reasonings, experiences misery after misery, like a thief, for he does something forbidden.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who identifies himself with the objective universe which has been denied by hundreds of Shrutis, Smritis and reasonings, experiences misery after misery, like a thief, for he does something forbidden.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्याभिसंधानरतो विमुक्तो महत्त्वमात्मीयमुपैति नित्यम् ।
मिथ्याभिसन्धानरतस्तु नश्येद् दृष्टं तदेतद्यदचौरचौरयोः ॥ ३३२ ॥
transliteration:
satyābhisaṃdhānarato vimukto mahattvamātmīyamupaiti nityam |
mithyābhisandhānaratastu naśyed dṛṣṭaṃ tadetadyadacauracaurayoḥ || 332 ||
translation: He who has devoted himself to meditation on the Reality (Brahman) and is free from Nescience, attains to the eternal glory of the Ātman. But he who dwells on the unreal (the universe) is destroyed. That this is so is evidenced in the case of one who is not a thief and one who is a thief.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who has devoted himself to meditation on the Reality (Brahman) and is free from Nescience, attains to the eternal glory of the Ātman. But he who dwells on the unreal (the universe) is destroyed. That this is so is evidenced in the case of one who is not a thief and one who is a thief.

sanskrit_shloka:
यतिरसदनुसन्धिं बन्धहेतुं विहाय स्वयमायामहमस्मीत्यात्मदृष्ट्यैव तिष्ठेत् ।
सुखयति ननु निष्ठा ब्रह्मणि स्वानुभूत्या हरति परमविद्याकार्यदुःखं प्रतीतम् ॥ ३३३ ॥
transliteration:
yatirasadanusandhiṃ bandhahetuṃ vihāya svayaMāyāmahamasmītyātmadṛṣṭyaiva tiṣṭhet |
sukhayati nanu niṣṭhā brahmaṇi svānubhūtyā harati paramavidyākāryaduḥkhaṃ pratītam || 333 ||
translation: The Sannyasin should give up dwelling on the unreal, which causes bondage, and should always fix his thoughts on the Ātman as 'I myself am This'. For the steadfastness in Brahman through the realisation of one’s identity with It gives rise to bliss and thoroughly removes the misery born of nescience, which one experiences (in the ignorant state).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Sannyasin should give up dwelling on the unreal, which causes bondage, and should always fix his thoughts on the Ātman as 'I myself am This'. For the steadfastness in Brahman through the realisation of one’s identity with It gives rise to bliss and thoroughly removes the misery born of nescience, which one experiences (in the ignorant state).

sanskrit_shloka:
बाह्यानुसन्धिः परिवर्धयेत्फलं दुर्वासनामेव ततस्ततोऽधिकाम् ।
ज्ञात्वा विवेकैः परिहृत्य बाह्यं स्वात्मानुसन्धिं विदधीत नित्यम् ॥ ३३४ ॥
transliteration:
bāhyānusandhiḥ parivardhayetphalaṃ durvāsanāmeva tatastato'dhikām |
jñātvā vivekaiḥ parihṛtya bāhyaṃ svātmānusandhiṃ vidadhīta nityam || 334 ||
translation: The dwelling on external objects will only intensify its fruits, viz. furthering evil propensities, which grow worse and worse. Knowing this through discrimination, one should avoid external objects and constantly apply oneself to meditation on the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The dwelling on external objects will only intensify its fruits, viz. furthering evil propensities, which grow worse and worse. Knowing this through discrimination, one should avoid external objects and constantly apply oneself to meditation on the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
बाह्ये निरुद्धे मनसः प्रसन्नता मनःप्रसादे परमात्मदर्शनम् ।
तस्मिन्सुदृष्टे भवबन्धनाशो बहिर्निरोधः पदवी विमुक्तेः ॥ ३३५ ॥
transliteration:
bāhye niruddhe manasaḥ prasannatā manaḥprasāde paramātmadarśanam |
tasminsudṛṣṭe bhavabandhanāśo bahirnirodhaḥ padavī vimukteḥ || 335 ||
translation: When the external world is shut out, the mind is cheerful, and cheerfulness of the mind brings on the vision of the Paramātman. When It is perfectly realised, the chain of birth and death is broken. Hence the shutting out of the external world is the stepping- stone to Liberation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the external world is shut out, the mind is cheerful, and cheerfulness of the mind brings on the vision of the Paramātman. When It is perfectly realised, the chain of birth and death is broken. Hence the shutting out of the external world is the stepping- stone to Liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
कः पण्डितः सन्सदसद्विवेकी श्रुतिप्रमाणः परमार्थदर्शी ।
जानन्हि कुर्यादसतोऽवलम्बं स्वपातहेतोः शिशुवन्मुमुक्षुः ॥ ३३६ ॥
transliteration:
kaḥ paṇḍitaḥ sansadasadvivekī śrutipramāṇaḥ paramārthadarśī |
jānanhi kuryādasato'valambaṃ svapātahetoḥ śiśuvanmumukṣuḥ || 336 ||
translation: Where is the man who being learned, able to discriminate the real from the unreal, believing the Vedas as authority, fixing his gaze on the Ātman, the Supreme Reality, and being a seeker after Liberation, will, like a child, consciously have recourse to the unreal (the universe) which will cause his fall?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Where is the man who being learned, able to discriminate the real from the unreal, believing the Vedas as authority, fixing his gaze on the Ātman, the Supreme Reality, and being a seeker after Liberation, will, like a child, consciously have recourse to the unreal (the universe) which will cause his fall?

sanskrit_shloka:
देहादिसंसक्तिमतो न मुक्तिः मुक्तस्य देहाद्यभिमत्यभावः ।
सुप्तस्य नो जागरणं न जाग्रतः स्वप्नस्तयोर्भिन्नगुणाश्रयत्वात् ॥ ३३७ ॥
transliteration:
dehādisaṃsaktimato na muktiḥ muktasya dehādyabhimatyabhāvaḥ |
suptasya no jāgaraṇaṃ na jāgrataḥ svapnastayorbhinnaguṇāśrayatvāt || 337 ||
translation: There is no Liberation for one who has attachment to the body etc., and the liberated man has no identification with the body etc. The sleeping man is not awake, nor is the waking man asleep, for these two states are contradictory in nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is no Liberation for one who has attachment to the body etc., and the liberated man has no identification with the body etc. The sleeping man is not awake, nor is the waking man asleep, for these two states are contradictory in nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
अन्तर्बहिः स्वं स्थिरजङ्गमेषु ज्ञात्वात्मनाधारतया विलोक्य ।
त्यक्ताखिलोपाधिरखण्डरूपः पूर्णात्मना यः स्थित एष मुक्तः ॥ ३३८ ॥
transliteration:
antarbahiḥ svaṃ sthirajaṅgameṣu jñātvātmanādhāratayā vilokya |
tyaktākhilopādhirakhaṇḍarūpaḥ pūrṇātmanā yaḥ sthita eṣa muktaḥ || 338 ||
translation: He is free who, knowing through his mind the Self in moving and unmoving objects and observing It as their substratum, gives up all superimpositions and remains as the Absolute and the infinite Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He is free who, knowing through his mind the Self in moving and unmoving objects and observing It as their substratum, gives up all superimpositions and remains as the Absolute and the infinite Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वात्मना बन्धविमुक्तिहेतुः सर्वात्मभावान्न परोऽस्ति कश्चित् ।
दृश्याग्रहे सत्युपपद्यतेऽसौ सर्वात्मभावोऽस्य सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥ ३३९ ॥
transliteration:
sarvātmanā bandhavimuktihetuḥ sarvātmabhāvānna paro'sti kaścit |
dṛśyāgrahe satyupapadyate'sau sarvātmabhāvo'sya sadātmaniṣṭhayā || 339 ||
translation: To realise the whole universe as the Self is the means of getting rid of bondage. There is nothing higher than identifying the universe with the Self. One realises this state by excluding the objective world through steadfastness in the eternal Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To realise the whole universe as the Self is the means of getting rid of bondage. There is nothing higher than identifying the universe with the Self. One realises this state by excluding the objective world through steadfastness in the eternal Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
दृश्यस्याग्रहणं कथं नु घटते देहात्मना तिष्ठतो बाह्यार्थानुभवप्रसक्तमनसस्तत्तत्क्रियां कुर्वतः ।
संन्यस्ताखिलधर्मकर्मविषयैर्नित्यात्मनिष्ठापरैः तत्त्वज्ञैः करणीयमात्मनि सदानन्देच्छुभिर्यत्नतः ॥ ३४0 ॥
transliteration:
dṛśyasyāgrahaṇaṃ kathaṃ nu ghaṭate dehātmanā tiṣṭhato bāhyārthānubhavaprasaktamanasastattatkriyāṃ kurvataḥ |
saṃnyastākhiladharmakarmaviṣayairnityātmaniṣṭhāparaiḥ tattvajñaiḥ karaṇīyamātmani sadānandecchubhiryatnataḥ || 340 ||
translation: How is the exclusion of the objective world possible for one who lives identified with the body, whose mind is attached to the perception of external objects, and who performs various acts for that end? This exclusion should be carefully practised by sages who have renounced all kinds of duties and actions and objects, who are passionately devoted to the eternal Ātman, and who wish to possess an undying bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How is the exclusion of the objective world possible for one who lives identified with the body, whose mind is attached to the perception of external objects, and who performs various acts for that end? This exclusion should be carefully practised by sages who have renounced all kinds of duties and actions and objects, who are passionately devoted to the eternal Ātman, and who wish to possess an undying bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वात्मसिद्धये भिक्षोः कृतश्रवणकर्मणः ।
समाधिं विदधात्येषा शान्तो दान्त इति श्रुतिः ॥ ३४१ ॥
transliteration:
sarvātmasiddhaye bhikṣoḥ kṛtaśravaṇakarmaṇaḥ |
samādhiṃ vidadhātyeṣā śānto dānta iti śrutiḥ || 341 ||
translation: To the Sannyasin who has gone through the act of hearing, the Shruti passage, 'Calm, self-controlled.' Etc., prescribes Samadhi for realising the identity of the universe with the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To the Sannyasin who has gone through the act of hearing, the Shruti passage, 'Calm, self-controlled.' Etc., prescribes Samadhi for realising the identity of the universe with the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
आरूढशक्तेरहमो विनाशः कर्तुन्न शक्य सहसापि पण्डितैः ।
ये निर्विकल्पाख्यसमाधिनिश्चलाः तानन्तरानन्तभवा हि वासनाः ॥ ३४२ ॥
transliteration:
ārūḍhaśakterahamo vināśaḥ kartunna śakya sahasāpi paṇḍitaiḥ |
ye nirvikalpākhyasamādhiniścalāḥ tānantarānantabhavā hi vāsanāḥ || 342 ||
translation: Even wise men cannot suddenly destroy egoism after it has once become strong, barring those who are perfectly calm through the Nirvikalpa Samadhi. Desires are verily the effect of innumerable births.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Even wise men cannot suddenly destroy egoism after it has once become strong, barring those who are perfectly calm through the Nirvikalpa Samadhi. Desires are verily the effect of innumerable births.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहंबुद्ध्यैव मोहिन्या योजयित्वावृतेर्बलात् ।
विक्षेपशक्तिः पुरुषं विक्षेपयति तद्गुणैः ॥ ३४३ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃbuddhyaiva mohinyā yojayitvāvṛterbalāt |
vikṣepaśaktiḥ puruṣaṃ vikṣepayati tadguṇaiḥ || 343 ||
translation: The projecting power, through the aid of the veiling power, connects a man with the siren of an egoistic idea, and distracts him through the attributes of that.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The projecting power, through the aid of the veiling power, connects a man with the siren of an egoistic idea, and distracts him through the attributes of that.

sanskrit_shloka:
विक्षेपशक्तिविजयो विषमो विधातुं निःशेषमावरणशक्तिनिवृत्त्यभावे ।
दृग्दृश्ययोः स्फुटपयोजलवद्विभागे नश्येत्तदावरणमात्मनि च स्वभावात् निःसंशयेन भवति प्रतिबन्धशून्यो विक्षेपणं नहिं तदा यदि चेन्मृषार्थे ॥ ३४४ ॥
transliteration:
vikṣepaśaktivijayo viṣamo vidhātuṃ niḥśeṣamāvaraṇaśaktinivṛttyabhāve |
dṛgdṛśyayoḥ sphuṭapayojalavadvibhāge naśyettadāvaraṇamātmani ca svabhāvāt niḥsaṃśayena bhavati pratibandhaśūnyo vikṣepaṇaṃ nahiṃ tadā yadi cenmṛṣārthe || 344 ||
translation: It is extremely difficult to conquer the projecting power unless the veiling power is perfectly rooted out. And that covering over the Ātman naturally vanishes when the subject is perfectly distinguished from the objects, like milk from water. But the victory is undoubtedly (complete and) free from obstacles when there is no oscillation of the mind due to the unreal sense-objects.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is extremely difficult to conquer the projecting power unless the veiling power is perfectly rooted out. And that covering over the Ātman naturally vanishes when the subject is perfectly distinguished from the objects, like milk from water. But the victory is undoubtedly (complete and) free from obstacles when there is no oscillation of the mind due to the unreal sense-objects.

sanskrit_shloka:
सम्यग्विवेकः स्फुटबोधजन्यो विभज्य दृग्दृश्यपदार्थतत्त्वम् ।
छिनत्ति मायाकृतमोहबन्धं यस्माद्विमुक्तस्तु पुनर्न संसृतिः ॥ ३४५ ॥
transliteration:
samyagvivekaḥ sphuṭabodhajanyo vibhajya dṛgdṛśyapadārthatattvam |
chinatti māyākṛtamohabandhaṃ yasmādvimuktastu punarna saṃsṛtiḥ || 345 ||
translation: Perfect discrimination brought on by direct realisation distinguishes the true nature of the subject from that of the object, and breaks the bond of delusion created by Māyā; and there is no more transmigration for one who has been freed from this.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Perfect discrimination brought on by direct realisation distinguishes the true nature of the subject from that of the object, and breaks the bond of delusion created by Māyā; and there is no more transmigration for one who has been freed from this.

sanskrit_shloka:
परावरैकत्वविवेकवन्हिः दहत्यविद्यागहनं ह्यशेषम् ।
किं स्यात्पुनः संसरणस्य बीजं अद्वैतभावं समुपेयुषोऽस्य ॥ ३४६ ॥
transliteration:
parāvaraikatvavivekavanhiḥ dahatyavidyāgahanaṃ hyaśeṣam |
kiṃ syātpunaḥ saṃsaraṇasya bījaṃ advaitabhāvaṃ samupeyuṣo'sya || 346 ||
translation: The knowledge of the identity of the Jiva and Brahman entirely consumes the impenetrable forest of Avidya or Nescience. For one who has realised the state of Oneness, is there any seed left for future transmigration?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The knowledge of the identity of the Jiva and Brahman entirely consumes the impenetrable forest of Avidya or Nescience. For one who has realised the state of Oneness, is there any seed left for future transmigration?

sanskrit_shloka:
आवरणस्य निवृत्तिर्भवति हि सम्यक्पदार्थदर्शनतः ।
मिथ्याज्ञानविनाशस्तद्विक्षेपजनितदुःखनिवृत्तिः ॥ ३४७ ॥
transliteration:
āvaraṇasya nivṛttirbhavati hi samyakpadārthadarśanataḥ |
mithyājñānavināśastadvikṣepajanitaduḥkhanivṛttiḥ || 347 ||
translation: The veil that hides Truth vanishes only when the Reality is fully realised. (Thence follow) the destruction of false knowledge and the cessation of misery brought about by its distracting influence.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The veil that hides Truth vanishes only when the Reality is fully realised. (Thence follow) the destruction of false knowledge and the cessation of misery brought about by its distracting influence.

sanskrit_shloka:
एतत्त्रितयं दृष्टं सम्यग्रज्जुस्वरूपविज्ञानात् ।
तस्माद्वस्तुसतत्त्वं ज्ञातव्यं बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ॥ ३४८ ॥
transliteration:
etattritayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ samyagrajjusvarūpavijñānāt |
tasmādvastusatattvaṃ jñātavyaṃ bandhamuktaye viduṣā || 348 ||
translation: These three are observed in the case of a rope when its real nature is fully known. Therefore the wise man should know the real nature of things for the breaking of his bonds.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: These three are observed in the case of a rope when its real nature is fully known. Therefore the wise man should know the real nature of things for the breaking of his bonds.

sanskrit_shloka:
अयोऽग्नियोगादिव सत्समन्वयान् मात्रादिरूपेण विजृम्भते धीः ।
तत्कार्यमेतद्द्वितयं यतो मृषा दृष्टं भ्रमस्वप्नमनोरथेषु ॥ ३४९ ॥
transliteration:
ततो विकाराः प्रकृतेरहंमुखा देहावसाना विषयाश्च सर्वे ।
क्षणेऽन्यथाभावितया ह्यमीषाम् असत्त्वमात्मा तु कदापि नान्यथा ॥ ३५0 ॥
translation: 349-350. Like iron manifesting as sparks through contact with fire, the Buddhi manifests itself as knower and known through the inherence of Brahman. As these two (knower and known), the effects of the Buddhi, are observed to be unreal in the case of delusion, dream and fancy, similarly, the modifications of the Prakriti, from egoism down to the body and all sense-objects are also unreal. Their unreality is verily due to their being subject to change every moment. But the Ātman never changes.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 349-350. Like iron manifesting as sparks through contact with fire, the Buddhi manifests itself as knower and known through the inherence of Brahman. As these two (knower and known), the effects of the Buddhi, are observed to be unreal in the case of delusion, dream and fancy, similarly, the modifications of the Prakriti, from egoism down to the body and all sense-objects are also unreal. Their unreality is verily due to their being subject to change every moment. But the Ātman never changes.

sanskrit_shloka:
नित्याद्वयाखण्डचिदेकरूपो बुद्ध्यादिसाक्षी सदसद्विलक्षणः ।
अहंपदप्रत्ययलक्षितार्थः प्रत्यक्सदानन्दघनः परात्मा ॥ ३५१ ॥
transliteration:
nityādvayākhaṇḍacidekarūpo buddhyādisākṣī sadasadvilakṣaṇaḥ |
ahaṃpadapratyayalakṣitārthaḥ pratyaksadānandaghanaḥ parātmā || 351 ||
translation: The Supreme Self is ever of the nature of eternal, indivisible knowledge, one without a second, the Witness of the Buddhi and the rest, distinct from the gross and subtle, the implied meaning of the term and idea 'I', the embodiment of inward, eternal bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Supreme Self is ever of the nature of eternal, indivisible knowledge, one without a second, the Witness of the Buddhi and the rest, distinct from the gross and subtle, the implied meaning of the term and idea 'I', the embodiment of inward, eternal bliss.
